searchText: Continue on my branch, 10.14 doesn't have all the code yet <@!199561711278227457> Could you update prysm to this? yup, on it 🙂 Nimbus evidently is proposing fine -- so why is https://consensusmonitor.kintsugi.themerge.dev/ still indicating its heads are weeks out of date? Might be co-related to a nimbus update, the consensus monitor doesn't handle updates too well currently. <@!131476523050860545> could you restart the consensus monitor once to see if it fixes the issue? restarting Also, `Nimbus Geth (0) Nimbus/v1.5.5-e62309-stateofus` etc (the cluster of four Nimbus entries at the bottom of the consensus monitor list) seems never to have run? <@!363800010518822915> Prysm syncs fine, but it keeps outputting these errors for me: ``` [2022-01-04 12:35:48] INFO blockchain: Synced new block blockRoot=0x341fa10f... epoch=4261 finalizedEpoch=4259 finalizedRoot=0x8abb0189... parentRoot=0x341fa10f... slot=136354 slotInEpoch=2 version=merge [2022-01-04 12:35:48] INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=27 slot=136354 [2022-01-04 12:35:49] INFO powchain: Connected to eth1 proof-of-work chain endpoint=http://localhost:8546 [2022-01-04 12:35:49] ERROR powchain: Unable to retrieve genesis ETH1.0 chain header: not found ``` You can ignore those for now, they are pretty much cosmetic <@!476250636548308992> Just noticed that if I shutdown geth and let prysm run for a bit without EL and restart geth, then prysm will not continue to sync. I think I have seen similar behavior on Lighthouse as well This is correct. It's a bug that we need to fix. We'll look into this soon Fyi in the latest commit, I have... - reenabled batch syncing, this speeds up the Prysm syncing to 4x-5x faster than before - hide the cosmetic errors when `--kintsugi-testnet` flag is applied ``` commit b45826e7317ffd0d5bf5a875d63d0e7d4e35b7f9 (HEAD -> kintsugi, origin/kintsugi) Author: terence tsao <terence@prysmaticlabs.com> Date: Tue Jan 4 10:15:40 2022 -0800 Speed up syncing, hide cosmetic errors ``` FWIW: are you connecting via RPC? I eventually had to switch from RPC to HTTP due to the former disconnecting and not being able reconnect (this made _some_ sense, but I was also running all of this over docker, which adds a layer of fuckery). I finally opted for HTTP
